claims: C1 developers may send any sequence of developer, user, and assistant messages as input, including assistant messages not actually generated by the assistant
C2 OpenAI may insert system messages into the input to steer the assistant's behavior
C3 developers receive the model's output messages from the API
C4 developers may not be aware of the existence or contents of the system messages
C5 developers may not receive hidden chain-of-thought messages generated by the assistant as part of producing its output messages

concepts.name: developer_definition
concepts.gloss: D is a customer of the OpenAI API who may add intelligence to software applications or create natural language interfaces consumed by end users

concepts.name: hidden_chain_of_thought_definition
concepts.gloss: C is a hidden chain-of-thought message generated by some of OpenAI's models to reason through a problem before generating a final answer, not exposed to the user or developer except potentially in summarized form

concepts.name: developer_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the developer role in the conversation
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of developer, user, and assistant messages as message roles; the role predicates are needed to express the sequence

concepts.name: user_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the user role in the conversation
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of developer, user, and assistant messages as message roles; the role predicates are needed to express the sequence

concepts.name: assistant_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the assistant role in the conversation
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of developer, user, and assistant messages as message roles; the role predicates are needed to express the sequence

concepts.name: assistant_generated
concepts.gloss: M is a message that was actually generated by the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause distinguishes assistant messages that were not actually generated by the assistant, so a predicate marking actual generation is needed

concepts.name: input_sequence
concepts.gloss: S is a sequence of messages that can be sent as input to the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of sending a sequence of messages as input; a predicate for such a sequence is needed

concepts.name: sequence_contains
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of a sequence of messages; membership in the sequence is needed to express which messages are included

concepts.name: system_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the system role inserted by OpenAI into the input
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of system messages inserted by OpenAI; a predicate for such messages is needed

concepts.name: steers_behavior
concepts.gloss: system message M steers the assistant's behavior
concepts.inference: the clause says OpenAI may insert system messages to steer behavior; a predicate linking the message to the steering purpose is needed

concepts.name: output_message
concepts.gloss: O is a message produced by the model and returned from the API
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of the model's output messages from the API; a predicate for such messages is needed

concepts.name: produced_as_part_of_output
concepts.gloss: C is a hidden chain-of-thought message generated by the assistant as part of producing output message O
concepts.inference: the clause says hidden chain-of-thought messages are generated as part of producing output messages; a relation between the hidden message and the output is needed

asserts.read_back: sending sequence % is permitted: it is a sequence of developer, user, and assistant messages
inserting system message % is permitted: OpenAI may insert it to steer the assistant's behavior
receiving output message % is permitted: developers receive the model's output messages from the API
being aware of system message % is not required: developers may not be aware of its existence or contents
receiving hidden chain-of-thought message % is not required: developers may not receive it

closure.reason: the clause explicitly permits sending any sequence of developer, user, and assistant messages; silence about other sequences leaves them permitted
the clause explicitly permits OpenAI to insert system messages; silence about other insertions leaves them permitted
the clause states developers receive output messages; it does not forbid receiving them, so silence permits
the clause says developers may not be aware of system messages, which is a statement of fact rather than a prohibition; it does not forbid awareness, so silence permits
the clause says developers may not receive hidden chain-of-thought messages, which is a statement of fact rather than a prohibition; it does not forbid receiving them, so silence permits
